record.context_brief: Largest dimension with the wedge bound
record.original_question: Let C be one of the following matrix classes: (i) the class of matrices A_{n,k,t} for positive integers n and k and t in (0, 1), (ii) the class of GKK τ-matrices, (iii) the class of GKK matrices, or (iv) the class of τ-matrices. For each n, let C_n denote the subclass of matrices in C whose order is at most n. What is the largest integer n such that every matrix in C_n satisfies the spectral wedge inequality |arg(λ - l(A))| ≤ π/2 - π/n for every eigenvalue λ of A?

evidence.quote: Mehrmann [12] showed that τ -matrices of order up to 4 satisfy the inequality | arg(λ − l(A))| ≤ π/2 − π/n ∀λ ∈ σ(A), (2), which is a property stronger than stability.
3b. What is the maximum n such that all matrices in class Cn satisfy (2)?

Specific classes C of interest include i. The class of matrices An,k,t for positive integers n and k, and for t ∈ (0, 1), ii. The class of GKK τ -matrices, iii. The class of GKK matrices, iv. The class of τ -matrices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a complex square matrix $A$ of order $n$, let $\sigma(A)$ denote its spectrum and let
$$l(A) = \min\{\operatorname{Re}\lambda : \lambda \in \sigma(A)\}.$$
Say that $A$ satisfies the wedge inequality if
$$\bigl|\arg(\lambda - l(A))\bigr| \le \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{n} \quad \text{for every } \lambda \in \sigma(A),$$
with the convention $\arg 0 = 0$.

Recall the following matrix classes:
\begin{itemize}
\item A real matrix $A$ is a \emph{GKK matrix} if every principal minor of $A$ is positive and, for every pair of disjoint nonempty index sets $\alpha, \beta \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|$, the product $A[\alpha\mid\beta]\cdot A[\beta\mid\alpha]$ of the corresponding minors is nonnegative.
\item A real matrix $A$ is a \emph{$\tau$-matrix} if for every $k=1,\dots,n$, every coefficient of $z^{n-k}$ in the characteristic polynomial $\det(zI-A)$, equal to $(-1)^k$ times the sum of all $k\times k$ principal minors of $A$, is positive (equivalently, all elementary symmetric functions of the eigenvalues are positive).
\item A \emph{GKK $\tau$-matrix} is a matrix that is both GKK and a $\tau$-matrix.
\item For positive integers $n,k$ and $t\in(0,1)$, let $A_{n,k,t}$ denote the $n\times n$ Toeplitz Hessenberg matrix whose entries on the main diagonal are $1$, on the first superdiagonal are $-1$, on the $j$-th subdiagonal ($1\le j\le k$) are $t^{j}$, and zero elsewhere.
\end{itemize}

For a class $\mathcal{C}$ of square matrices and a positive integer $n$, let $\mathcal{C}_n$ denote the set of matrices in $\mathcal{C}$ of order at most $n$.

For each of the following classes $\mathcal{C}$, determine the largest integer $n$ (if any) such that every matrix in $\mathcal{C}_n$ satisfies the wedge inequality:
(i) $\mathcal{C} = \{A_{n,k,t} : n,k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0},\ t\in(0,1)\}$;
(ii) $\mathcal{C}$ = the class of GKK $\tau$-matrices;
(iii) $\mathcal{C}$ = the class of GKK matrices;
(iv) $\mathcal{C}$ = the class of $\tau$-matrices.
artifact.status_search_result: The wedge inequality was established for orders n ≤ 3 (Varga; Hershkowitz–Berman) and for n = 4 (Mehrmann), and counterexamples to stability (a weaker property) are known for GKK τ-matrices of the form A_{2k+2,k,t} for sufficiently large k. However, no explicit determination of the largest n for which the wedge inequality holds for the four classes appears to have been published, and the problem is still listed among open problems on GKK τ-matrices.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on GKK τ-matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Mehrmann showed that τ-matrices of order up to 4 satisfy the wedge inequality; the maximum n for which matrices in class C_n satisfy (2) is posed as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of the maximum n is posed and only verified up to n=4 for τ-matrices.

status_evidence.title: Theorems and counterexamples on structured matrices
status_evidence.snippet: A_{2k+2,k,t} is unstable for sufficiently large k and sufficiently small positive t, giving counterexamples to stability conjectures for GKK τ-matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples to stability (a weaker consequence of the wedge inequality) exist for GKK τ-matrices at high enough order; the exact threshold for the wedge inequality itself is not pinned down.
